leads.summary: Same-size edits within one stat-visible second still serve the old thumbnail
leads.consequence: The new fast signature, the full signature, and the thumbnail hash all use file size plus stat %Y (whole epoch seconds). An image whose bytes change but whose size and second-level mtime remain unchanged gets a fast row-cache hit and the original thumbnail path on every following open, even if its directory mtime is unchanged. Merely increasing the fast signature's precision without also changing thumbnail_for and shell/plugins/image-picker/list.sh:19-26 would still return the old .jpg. Consider a higher-resolution timestamp across all three consumers, or content/inotify-based invalidation if preserved timestamps must be covered.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; same-size same-second residual (Opus B2); published as pre-existing note in Details

leads.summary: The responsive-background PRs conflict with the relocated media filter
leads.consequence: Open #9312 changes the media walk to include .svg and exclude names containing @ (responsive variants), and #9313 builds on it. This PR deletes the old cold-walk lines and moves that walk before the fast-cache decision. A three-way merge against #9312's own base produced a conflict at merged line 145, as did #9313; keeping this PR's walk drops SVG wallpapers and shows variant files as independent picker items, while keeping the old walk loses the per-file fast signature. When integrating, carry both filters into the single pre-cache sweep, retain #9312's thumbnail timeout, and test an SVG plus an @ variant and an in-place edit. These are prospective integrations, not defects in the currently pinned head.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_coordinator; #9312 edits the same find filter in the moved block; gh pr diff 9312 by coordinator, merge-tree conflict confirmed in Opus self-check (opus/draft-check/pr-9312.diff)

leads.summary: At current quattro, shell-held theme rows can still open with old thumbnails before refresh
leads.consequence: Since #13403, the theme picker opens from themeRows already held by the shell (287-300) and starts omarchy-theme-switcher --print-rows asynchronously afterward (302-335). If a preview changes in place after the previous refresh, this PR's new signature takes effect only when that background process completes; an initial opening may present the old thumbnail even after merging, then update to the new path at lines 313-319 if the rows differ. The existing background picker passes directly through the script, so this distinction is theme-specific. Whether stale pixels are actually rendered before refresh requires visual observation, unavailable in this assignment. Document or test that asynchronous opening behavior before claiming instant freshness on current quattro.
leads.triage: dropped; QML held-rows first-open staleness is #13403 design, pre-existing and not PR-specific; Opus Q5 covered consumers; not observable without desktop

leads.summary: Each newly invalidated in-place edit leaves its prior thumbnail and index row behind
leads.consequence: For each changed size or timestamp, thumbnail_for appends another index.tsv entry and generates another hash.jpg. The only cleanup on a successful row-cache publish concerns temporary row files, not earlier thumbnails or the old index entries. Repeated in-place saves now generate fresh entries where the old directory-only fast hit would have reused one, and the per-user cache grows without bound until external cleanup. A two-version fixture retained both jpgs and both index rows. If normal editing volume is material, bound/evict unreferenced versions while respecting other directory keys and the direct picker consumer.
leads.triage: dropped; index/thumbnail accumulation pre-existing in thumbnail_for; low value

leads.summary: PR #13242 independently changes the same v4 cache-sweep hunk and cannot be applied atop this PR
leads.consequence: Both open PRs fix #11806 using per-file size and mtime in the fast signature, but #13242 preserves a separate cold-only full scan and extracts an image_name_filters array, whereas this PR builds fast/full signatures in one pass. The other PR's patch fails both hunks against this head, and merge-file against its own merge-base yields three conflicts in the signature block. Do not blindly concatenate both implementations, choose one walk and retain the relevant tests, or close the duplicate. This is a merge conflict, not an additional end-user runtime regression if a correct single implementation is chosen.

leads.summary: The current quattro test appends a second EOF case, so the test file needs a conflict resolution
leads.consequence: The head-side overwrite regression and the newer base's --print-rows case both append after the same final test. A three-way merge against 86a2e58 reports conflict markers at lines 145-187 of the merged test, although the production script merges cleanly. Concatenating both cases after resolving the hunk preserves behavior, and the combined fixture passed on the merged production file. This is an integration chore, not evidence of a production logic conflict.

leads.summary: The new regression test has no unchanged-tree warm-hit assertion
leads.consequence: The added test checks only that a changed-size overwrite produces a different thumbnail path. Disabling both row-cache hit decisions completely still makes every assertion in the entire patched menu-images test pass, even though every unchanged invocation now rebuilds rows and rewrites signatures. The PR moved all directory and per-file work before the cache decision, so protecting the warm-hit path is pertinent. Add a third invocation without editing the image and assert that cached rows are reused (for example, unchanged row inode and no extra index lookup), then change the image and assert invalidation.

leads.summary: The rewritten failed-video comment misstates what the signatures include
leads.consequence: The new comment says a signature would describe 'only the remaining successful rows', but both signatures are assembled from all files before thumbnail_for runs, including a file whose video conversion fails (lines 130-134). A changed size/mtime on a repaired video would invalidate even such a signature; an unchanged-size/mtime video stays rejected via thumbnail.failed even without a row-cache hit. The uncached choice still protects incomplete batches and timeout retries. Reword the comment around those actual reasons, rather than suggesting signatures omit failed media.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Every warm open of the picker now runs one `stat` process per image, which undoes most of the fast signature's saving.

### Cache hits now stat every image

The file sweep moved before the cache decision, so a row-cache hit now forks `stat -Lc '%s:%Y'` once per media file (`bin/omarchy-menu-images` line 132) instead of one `stat` on the directory. With a stub thumbnailer, warm opens took 9 to 10 ms at the merge-base for 10, 100 or 1000 images, and 18, 82 and 704 ms at this head. **Impact:** opening the Background picker on a large wallpaper folder is delayed by about 0.7 ms per file; stock themes (2 to 9 images) add at most about 9 ms.

**Suggested change:** Build the file list and signatures from a single `find -L ... -printf '%s:%T@\t%p\0' | sort -z -t $'\t' -k 2` sweep, which kept the fix and measured 12/14/41 ms.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 2cc37f0)</summary>

##### Test case

Append to `test/shell.d/menu-images-test.sh` (uses the file's own `$tmp`, `$cache_home`, `$images`, `$stub_bin` and helpers):

```bash
# A warm open should cost the same few processes however many images there are.
rm -rf "$cache_home"
mkdir -p "$cache_home"
PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$cache_home" \
  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-menu-images" --cache-only "$images"

real_stat=$(type -P stat)
cat >"$stub_bin/stat" <<EOF_STAT
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >>"\$STAT_CALLS_FILE"
exec "$real_stat" "\$@"
EOF_STAT
chmod +x "$stub_bin/stat"
: >"$tmp/stat-calls"
PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$cache_home" STAT_CALLS_FILE="$tmp/stat-calls" \
  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-menu-images" --cache-only "$images"
rm "$stub_bin/stat"

(( $(wc -l <"$tmp/stat-calls") == 1 )) ||
  fail "a warm image menu open does not stat each image" "$(<"$tmp/stat-calls")"
pass "a warm image menu open does not stat each image"
```

Actual output at head (stderr of the failing case; exit status 1):

```text
-Lc %Y /tmp/tmp.TpBzYR4sur/images
-Lc %s:%Y /tmp/tmp.TpBzYR4sur/images/one.png
-Lc %s:%Y /tmp/tmp.TpBzYR4sur/images/three.png
-Lc %s:%Y /tmp/tmp.TpBzYR4sur/images/two.png
not ok - a warm image menu open does not stat each image
```

At the merge-base the same case prints `ok - a warm image menu open does not stat each image` (one `stat`, for the directory).

##### Warm-open timing

`bench.sh` (stub thumbnailer, private `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, mean of 10 warm `--cache-only` opens after one warming run):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: bench.sh path/to/bin/omarchy-menu-images
# Times warm (row-cache hit) opens with --cache-only and a stub thumbnailer.
set -euo pipefail

script=$1
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmp/bin"
cat >"$tmp/bin/vipsthumbnail" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
while (( $# > 0 )); do
  [[ $1 == "--path" ]] && { printf 'thumbnail' >"${2%%\[*}"; exit 0; }
  shift
done
STUB
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/vipsthumbnail"

open_menu() {
  PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$tmp/cache" "$script" --cache-only "$1"
}

for n in 10 100 1000; do
  dir="$tmp/images-$n"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do printf 'image %d' "$i" >"$dir/$i.png"; done
  open_menu "$dir"
  start=${EPOCHREALTIME/./}
  for (( r = 0; r < 10; r++ )); do open_menu "$dir"; done
  end=${EPOCHREALTIME/./}
  printf '%4d images: %4d ms per warm open\n' "$n" $(( (end - start) / 10000 ))
done
```

Actual output, merge-base script:

```text
  10 images:    9 ms per warm open
 100 images:   10 ms per warm open
1000 images:   10 ms per warm open
```

Actual output, head script:

```text
  10 images:   18 ms per warm open
 100 images:   82 ms per warm open
1000 images:  704 ms per warm open
```

Actual output, head script with the single-`find` sweep below:

```text
  10 images:   12 ms per warm open
 100 images:   14 ms per warm open
1000 images:   41 ms per warm open
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

##### Single-find variant used above

```diff
--- a/bin/omarchy-menu-images
+++ b/bin/omarchy-menu-images
@@ -127,15 +127,18 @@
     rows_fast_signature+="$dir:$dir_mtime"$'\n'
     rows_signature+="$dir:$dir_mtime"$'\n'
 
-    while IFS= read -r -d '' image; do
+    # One find reports each file's size and mtime (the link target's, under
+    # -L), so the sweep is one process rather than one stat per file. Sort on
+    # the path field only, so row order stays what sorting paths gave.
+    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
+      image=${entry#*$'\t'}
       image_files+=("$image")
-      image_signature=$(stat -Lc '%s:%Y' "$image") || continue
-      rows_fast_signature+="$image:$image_signature"$'\n'
-      rows_signature+="$image:$image_signature"$'\n'
+      rows_fast_signature+="$image:${entry%%$'\t'*}"$'\n'
+      rows_signature+="$image:${entry%%$'\t'*}"$'\n'
     done < <(find -L "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
       \( -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.jpeg' -o -iname '*.png' -o -iname '*.gif' -o -iname '*.bmp' -o -iname '*.webp' \
          -o -iname '*.mp4' -o -iname '*.m4v' -o -iname '*.mov' -o -iname '*.webm' -o -iname '*.mkv' -o -iname '*.avi' \) \
-      -print0 2>/dev/null | sort -z)
+      -printf '%s:%T@\t%p\0' 2>/dev/null | sort -z -t $'\t' -k 2)
   fi
 done
 
```

With this variant the PR's own test file passes (6 ok), plus the warm-open case above. Sorting on the path field keeps the row order identical to head under `C.UTF-8` and `en_US.UTF-8`; a variant that puts the path first (`%p\t%s:%T@`) reordered rows under `en_US.UTF-8` in the review's run. `%T@` has a fractional part, so the signature format changes and both version strings would need a bump if this is adopted.

**Verified** (sandbox, stub thumbnailer):
- A same-size overwrite with a new mtime second, a replaced symlink target, and an overwrite in a second directory all get a new thumbnail at head (the same row at the merge-base).
- A stale cache written by the old code is rebuilt; an unchanged tree cached by the old code keeps its rows (the full signature still matches).
- The PR's test fails at the merge-base and passed 25 of 25 runs at head.

**Optional test improvement:** mutants that never take the fast hit, or always rebuild rows, still pass all 6 cases in the test file. The warm-open case in the Reproducer catches the always-rebuild one; checking that a second open leaves the `.rows` and `.fast-signature` files untouched would catch both.

Not covered by this PR and pre-existing: an overwrite that keeps the same size and the same whole-second mtime is still not detected, because `thumbnail_for` keys thumbnails on the same `size:mtime` value.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

#### The rewritten `.failed` comment gives a reason that is no longer true

Both signatures now include every media file with its size and mtime, including the failed video, so a cached batch would still be invalidated by an in-place repair. Keeping the batch uncached still matters for retrying once a `.failed` marker is removed without the file changing.

**Suggested change:** reword the comment along the lines of "The signatures already cover the failed video's size and mtime; the batch stays uncached so the video is retried once its .failed marker is gone."

The comment at head lines 275-277 says the batch must stay uncached because a signature "that still describes only the remaining successful rows" would hide a later in-place repair. With this PR both signatures list every media file found, including the failed video, with its size and mtime (head lines 130-134). The script below drops `rows_cacheable=false` from the `.failed` branch so the batch is cached, repairs the video in place with the directory mtime restored, and opens again.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: failed-repair.sh path/to/bin/omarchy-menu-images
# Lets a batch with a failed video be cached (drops rows_cacheable=false from
# the .failed branch), then repairs the video in place without changing the
# directory mtime, and reports whether the next open notices.
set -euo pipefail

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/images"
awk '
  after && /^[[:space:]]*rows_cacheable=false$/ { after = 0; next }
  { after = 0 }
  /if \[\[ \$thumbnail == \*\.failed \]\]; then$/ { after = 1 }
  { print }
' "$1" >"$tmp/bin/omarchy-menu-images"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/omarchy-menu-images"
cat >"$tmp/bin/ffmpegthumbnailer" <<STUB
#!/bin/bash
[[ -e $tmp/fail ]] && exit 1
while (( \$# > 0 )); do [[ \$1 == "-o" ]] && { printf 'thumbnail' >"\$2"; exit 0; }; shift; done
STUB
cat >"$tmp/bin/vipsthumbnail" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
while (( $# > 0 )); do [[ $1 == "--path" ]] && { printf 'thumbnail' >"${2%%\[*}"; exit 0; }; shift; done
STUB
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/ffmpegthumbnailer" "$tmp/bin/vipsthumbnail"

printf 'good' >"$tmp/images/good.png"
printf 'broken' >"$tmp/images/broken.mp4"
open_menu() { PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$tmp/cache" "$tmp/bin/omarchy-menu-images" --cache-only "$tmp/images"; }
rows="$tmp/cache/omarchy/image-selector/$(printf '%s' "$tmp/images" | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1).rows"

touch "$tmp/fail"
open_menu   # converter fails, .failed marker written
open_menu   # .failed branch taken; the mutated script caches the batch
[[ -f $rows ]] && echo "batch cached without the failed video: $(grep -c . "$rows") row(s)"

rm "$tmp/fail"
touch -r "$tmp/images" "$tmp/dir-mtime"
printf 'repaired video bytes' >"$tmp/images/broken.mp4"
touch -r "$tmp/dir-mtime" "$tmp/images"
open_menu

if grep -q 'broken.mp4' "$rows" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "in-place repair noticed: the video row is back"
else
  echo "in-place repair hidden: the video row is still missing"
fi
```

Actual output with the merge-base script:

```text
batch cached without the failed video: 1 row(s)
in-place repair hidden: the video row is still missing
```

Actual output with the head script:

```text
batch cached without the failed video: 1 row(s)
in-place repair noticed: the video row is back
```

So after this PR the repair is noticed even when the batch is cached; the uncached rule is no longer what protects it. This is a comment accuracy point, not a behaviour defect: the unmodified head script also notices the repair.

#### Test file conflict with current `quattro`

`quattro` commit 24f1243120 (#13403) appends a `--print-rows` case at the same place as this PR's new case. The script merges cleanly.

**Suggested change:** rebase and keep both test cases.

```text
$ git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/quattro pr-11882   # quattro 8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70, head 2cc37f0b07f4cf9c84185a03cb5bbc4c26ee7144
487a2335f7b6220e31437d7f5f4df53bcc8fe4a5
test/shell.d/menu-images-test.sh

Auto-merging bin/omarchy-menu-images
Auto-merging test/shell.d/menu-images-test.sh
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in test/shell.d/menu-images-test.sh
(exit status 1)
```

`bin/omarchy-menu-images` merges cleanly. The test conflict is two cases appended after the last one: quattro's `--print-rows` case from 24f1243120 (#13403) and this PR's in-place overwrite case. Keeping both resolves it; the resolved file passed 7 of 7 cases, and 25 of 25 repeated runs.
</details>

<details><summary>Other open PRs for this issue</summary>

- #13242 builds the same per-file fast signature (same warm-open cost) but keeps a second sweep on a cache miss (450 vs 366 ms at 100 images) and adds no test. It conflicts with this PR in `bin/omarchy-menu-images`, so only one can land.
- Overlapping, not the same issue: #9312 changes the same `find` filter (adds `*.svg`, excludes `*@*` names) inside the block this PR moves; a rebase of either needs to carry the filter change into the new sweep.
</details>
